text:
Maya Patel: @here quick heads-up: I'm proposing a change to the eu-west admit policy for GPU surges. Move from hard-reject (current) to a soft-queue + degrade path for silver/bronze traffic, keep gold on fastpath. Reason: reduce customer 5xx and avoid tail outages when AZs get saturated.

Raul Gomez: Can you share expected p99/impact? we need gold p99 < 2s at all times.

Maya Patel: Gold stays on the fastpath, no change. For silver/bronze: queue up to 2000ms, then switch to degrade (quantized model / shorter context / early token stop). Expected p99 for queued requests may hit ~3s in worst case, but errors drop a lot.

Sasha Lee: How does this interact with the autoscaler? if we queue instead of reject, autoscaler might spin up more nodes and cost will go up.

Ashwin Rao: We should gate autoscale on sustained queued-exec, not transient queue blips. Add a hysteresis window and a 'queue_to_reject' overflow threshold so we can still fail fast if it's runaway.

Maya Patel: Agreed. Proposed config snippet:```yaml
admit_policy:
  mode: soft_queue
  max_queue_ms: 2000
  degrade_mode: shorten-context-or-quantized
  priority_buckets: [gold, silver, bronze]
  queue_hysteresis_secs: 180
  queue_reject_threshold: 800  # queue length beyond which we revert to hard-reject
```

OpsBot: ALERT: eu-west GPU util 94% (5m avg), queue depth 310, dropping 1200rps reroutes.

Raul Gomez: Ok we need a canary. Suggest AZ1 only, short window, very explicit SLO gates:
- gold p99 < 2s
- overall error_rate delta <= +0.5%
- degrade_rate < 15% for silver
- cost_delta < +12% over baseline

Maya Patel: Canary plan: start tomorrow 03:30UTC in eu-west-1a, synthetic traffic ramp to 500rps over 30m, keep canary 45m. Metrics to watch: queue_latency, queue_depth, degrade_rate, gold_p99, 5xx_rate, autoscaler_scale_ops. Rollback if any gate violated.

Sasha Lee: Also add a circuit-breaker rule: if autoscaler_trigger_count > 3 within 10m, immediately revert to hard-reject to avoid runaway GPU billing.

Ashwin Rao: I'll attach a quick cost sim: expected +8% GPU-hours during peak for this pattern, but simulated error rate drops ~70% vs hard-reject for mixed-priority workloads. That delta probably justifies the extra hours for enterprise customers.

Maya Patel: We'll also enable a temporary cheaper degrade model variant (smaller quantized weights) to limit cost. Implementation notes: change admit controller to produce admit_response = {action: queue|accept_degrade|accept_fastpath|reject} and add metrics tags: admit.action, admit.reason, queue.wait_ms.

Raul Gomez: One more ask — include a per-customer max-queued-requests limit so a noisy tenant can't fill the queue.

Maya Patel: Good call. Add per-tenant queue cap and preferential eviction order (bronze first).

Sasha Lee: I'll prep the autoscaler changes and test in staging. Need a short PR for the admit controller + metric names.

Ashwin Rao: +1 from product side. I'll notify CS that bronze customers may see degraded output during the canary window.

Maya Patel: I'll open an RFC and the canary runbook now, and post links here when ready. /cc @Sasha Lee @Raul Gomez

Raul Gomez: Sounds good. Please include rollback KB and runbook triggers (manual + automated).

Maya Patel: Will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
